text: In 1940, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge was nicknamed Galloping Gertie before it even fell down. Nobody took the hint. The deck was thin and shallow, like a ribbon. Wind flowing around it made it twist, and each twist made the next one bigger. That's called flutter. Four months after it opened, the deck tore itself apart in a steady wind. Every big bridge since has been wind-tunnel tested. Engineers learned. Dave didn't.
